description: Full-text search across SEC filing content that returns the MATCHING PASSAGE: one match per filing, each with the exhibit it was found in (`exhibit_id`, `exhibit_type`) and the snippet with context. Query syntax: unquoted words must ALL appear (any order, any distance); "quoted phrase" = exact wording; OR between alternatives (merger OR acquisition); -word or -"phrase" to exclude; w1 NEAR/10 w2 (also NEAR(10), or bare NEAR = within 10) = words close together; word* = prefix of 4+ letters (dilut* matches dilution, dilutive); $AAPL or a capitalised ticker scopes to that company; a form code (8-K, 10-Q, S-1), "item 5.02" / "8-K 1.05" and a bare year (2024) scope to that form / 8-K item / year. Unquoted words match anywhere in the filing, so quote multi-word phrases. When the archive states how it read the query it is in meta.understanding. Best for locating specific clauses ("change of control", "anti-dilution", "right of first refusal") and for getting the excerpt for a known filing (pass accessionNumber or filingId). Use search_sec_filings with `q` instead when you need filing-level paging (cursor), totals, date ranges, 8-K item codes, excluded forms, or company filters. Optionally filter by company (CIK), filing, accession number, or form type, restrict matching to sections (section=risk_factors, mdna, ex99 …; confirmed by meta.sections, otherwise meta.unsupported says the whole filing was searched) and filter by exhibit type (exhibitTypes=EX-10). Coverage: Signal8's archive of SEC EDGAR filings in the archive's held range (see `archiveFrom` in each response; currently from late 2021, expanding back to 2016 as the history backfill fills in), updated through the day. The archive only holds filings from its `archiveFrom` date; before that it holds only a scatter (well under 1% of most years), so ABSENCE BEFORE archiveFrom IS NOT EVIDENCE a filing was never filed — check SEC EDGAR for earlier periods. Some rows are record-only (bodyStored: false — metadata from the EDGAR index with no document body), so their text cannot be read here; open them at their sec.gov URL.

accessionNumber.description: Filter to a specific filing by SEC accession number

cik.description: Filter to a specific company by CIK number

exhibitTypes.description: Keep only filings carrying ANY of these exhibit types (comma-separated): a family such as EX-10 (material contracts) matches every member (EX-10.1, EX-10.2…); an exact type such as EX-99.1 (usually the press release) only itself. Others: EX-97 clawback policy, EX-3 charter/bylaws, EX-4 instruments/warrants, EX-21 subsidiaries, EX-23 consents. "10.1" is accepted for EX-10.1. Listed in appliedFilters when the rows prove it; otherwise in ignoredFilters / meta.unsupported — treat the rows as unfiltered then.

facets.description: true = also return `facets` { forms, years, items } — [{ value, count }] over the whole match set. Absent when not measured (never zero). Default false.

filingId.description: Filter to a specific filing by internal ID

match.description: Word matching. exact = a word matches only itself ("split" does NOT match "splits") — EDGAR full-text search's behaviour; stemmed = English word variations also match. Default when omitted: stemmed. The mode actually applied is reported in the response's meta.matchMode.

matchedSections.description: Per-row `matchedSections` (default true): the sections the text matched in. ABSENT on a row means not measured (index without sections), never "matched nowhere".

pattern.description: Search query (minimum 2 characters): "exact phrase", OR, -exclude, w1 NEAR/n w2, word*, $TICKER. A CIK/filing-scoped search whose text is not indexed yet falls back to a literal case-insensitive substring match (response engine: "substring").

section.description: Restrict MATCHING to sections (comma-separated): business, risk_factors, cybersecurity, legal_proceedings, mdna, market_risk, controls (10-K/10-Q/20-F narrative items, by meaning — mdna is 10-K Item 7, 10-Q Part I Item 2 and 20-F Item 5), ex99 (press-release / EX-99.x exhibit text) and item_X_YY (the text under an 8-K item, e.g. item_5_02). Aliases: mda, risk, legal, cyber, press_release, 5.02. Unknown names are a 400. Needs q. Applied ONLY when the response's meta.sections names it — otherwise meta.unsupported says why (e.g. the archive index does not have sections yet) and matches may come from ANYWHERE in the filing.

snippetLength.description: Characters of context around each match (default: 200)

sort.description: Result order: newest (default) or relevance (best match first)

understand.description: Query understanding (default true): tickers/$TICKER, company names, form codes, "item N.NN" and synonym expansion, reported in meta.understanding. false = match the words literally.
